label: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 10
knowledgePattern: Use remainder values to identify a bounded-degree polynomial
solution:
The remainder theorem gives p(1)=1, p(2)=2 and p(4)=4. Together with p(0)=0, these show that q(x)=p(x)−x has the four distinct roots 0,1,2,4.

The degree of q is at most 3. A nonzero polynomial of degree at most 3 cannot have four distinct roots, so q is the zero polynomial. Hence p(x)=x, whose cubic coefficient is 0. Answer D.

hints.title: Translate remainders into values
hints.body: Evaluate the polynomial at each linear divisor’s zero and include the separate value supplied in the question.
hints.recap: The remainder on division by x minus a is the polynomial value at a.
hints.pitfall: Degree at most three does not require the cubic coefficient to be nonzero.
hints.pause: Look for a simple polynomial sharing all the supplied values.

hints.body: Subtract your candidate from p and count the distinct roots that the difference must have.
hints.recap: New learning: a nonzero polynomial of degree n has at most n distinct real roots.
hints.pitfall: The zero polynomial is the exception to the finite root bound.
hints.pause: Compare the root count with the degree bound and infer the requested coefficient.
